name: vibration-budget
description: Chapter 5: 3 catastrophic overcharge blasts crater nuisance and ecology scores. Finding #9: the file's original premise ("exceed vibration budget 3 times... verify $5,000 fine is applied") has no implementation anywhere in the codebase to test — recordVibration (ScoreManager.ts) only moves nuisance/ecology, no budget counter or cash fine exists, and no event/campaign rule ties one to blast count either. That claim is dropped here in favor of the real, checkable effect (nuisance/ecology cratering); whether a real fine mechanic should exist is a game-design question, out of scope for a test-assertion pass — filed as a follow-up, not silently implemented.

Cash bumped to $250,000: 3 catastrophic blasts each need a fresh driller+drill_rig (see below), $36,000 a cycle, on top of payroll/upkeep during 3 separate drilling waits.

steps.description: #553: drill_hole is now a queued, vehicle-gated action — a driller physically drives a drill_rig to each hole — so each of this file's 3 blast cycles now needs its own fresh crew: rumblox at this overcharge is genuinely lethal (Finding #9's honest premise), and the driller/drill_rig that just drilled a site routinely dies/is destroyed in its own blast (sandbox-measured), so a new one is hired for each grid rather than reused. Fired again right after each blast (see below) so a surviving-but-idle driller from an earlier cycle doesn't drag the roster's average wellbeing down across the whole file and risk a worker_revolt on cycle 3.

steps.description: Finding #9 (see file description): the original file charged explosive:boomite, whose maxChargeKg is 8 — amount:15 exceeds it, so batchCharge rejected the whole charge with an error, never applied, never thrown (success:false, silent). chargedCount stayed 0 through the entire charge/sequence/blast pipeline in every run of this file's history — no hole was ever actually charged, sequenced, or blasted, so the file never once produced the catastrophic overcharge it claims to test. Fixed by using rumblox instead — the catalog's own "defining trait: high vibration" product (vibrationMod 1.6, maxChargeKg 20, ExplosiveCatalog.ts), which is also the more honest real product for this file's stated intent. Finding #10: Charge All (chargeAll(), Charge.ts) issues `charge hole:* explosive:${this.selectedExplosiveId} amount:${this.amountKg}kg stemming:${this.stemmingM}m` from the panel's OWN selection state — selectedExplosiveId defaults to boomite (DEFAULT_EXPLOSIVE) and only changes when a product card is clicked (data-action="select-explosive", data-explosive="<id>"). A real browser run confirmed this: without clicking the rumblox card first, every one of this file's 3 charge-all clicks silently applied the panel's boomite/5kg/2m defaults instead of the declared rumblox/15kg/1m — producing a normal, non-catastrophic blast (nuisance barely moved, 50→49.975) instead of the intended overcharge. Fixed by clicking the rumblox product card, then driving the amount stepper 5→15kg (10 clicks, 1kg/click) and the stemming stepper 2→1m (5 clicks, 0.2m/click, data-field="amount"/"stemming") before Charge All — the same class of gap as Finding #4/#5, generalized to explosive selection.
#554: drain the charge order(s) queued by the step above (charging is real work, not instant) before continuing.

#554-followup (issue #586 CI): idempotent -- a no-op when nothing is pending, resolves one when a timer fired during the charge-drain wait above (up to 3000 ticks at 8x speed is real time long enough for a random event to land). Without this, a fired-and-unresolved event's own .bs-confirm-overlay backdrop blocks the next click -- real CI reported exactly that (the following `employee fire 1` step's own toolbar-open click never landed, leaving employeeCount at 2 instead of 1 by the checkpoint several steps later).

#601-followup: leading `resolveEventIfPending` added -- the preceding `event choose 0` step's own resolve and this step's first click are two separate real-time steps with a gap between them (each interaction-mode step incurs its own CDP round-trips); a timer event landing in that gap leaves its `.bs-confirm-overlay` backdrop covering the blast panel, failing this step's own `[data-step="3"]` click with "element is covered by div" -- confirmed via direct CI-reproducing run. Re-checking for a pending event as this step's own first action, immediately before the click that needs the panel clear, closes that race instead of relying on the earlier step's now-stale resolve.

steps.description: #601-followup: was `event choose 0` (resolveEventIfPending) then `employee fire 1`. Direct probe (deathCount right after the blast step above, both modes, run 3x each) shows grid 1's driller now dies deterministically in BOTH modes -- the file's old "not always" is stale, same staleness #601 already found and fixed for grid 2's own analogous transition (see that step's own note, several hundred lines below). A dead employee has no row in #bs-employee-panel (`CrewPanel.render` filters to `e.alive`) -- `.bs-detail-toggle` was never going to exist, so the old toggle/dismiss/confirm `clickIfPresent` chain always no-op'd in interaction mode. But `fireEmployee` (Employee.ts) splices by id with no `alive` check, so the OLD command-mode script (a bare `employee fire 1`) still spliced the corpse for real -- a real player has no click for that, since the row doesn't exist to click. That command-vs-interaction action-count asymmetry is what #601 traced for grid 2 (`runCommand`'s action-count gate charges `employee fire` whether it fires a live employee or a corpse, but interaction mode's genuine no-op charges nothing), and it applies here identically. Fixed the same way #601 fixed grid 2: `time resume` is idempotent this deep into an already-resumed run and, as a META_COMMAND, exempt from the action-count gate in both modes, so neither mode's replay of this step nudges the cooldown gate. The one remaining click -- opening the employees panel, so the hire step below still finds it open -- stays, modeling a player checking on their dead crew and finding nobody left to dismiss.

#553: a fresh driller for grid 2/3 — see grid 1's own hire step for why (a new one each cycle, fired after each blast). #553-followup: no toolbar click here -- the preceding `time resume` step already opened the employees panel (it clicks `#bs-toolbar [data-panel="employees"]` itself, see its own #601-followup note) and the `finances` step between it and this one is a command-only observe step that never touches panel state, so the panel is still open. ToolRail's click handler is a togglePanel toggle (UIManager.ts:450) -- re-clicking here closed the panel outright, leaving the driller row zero-size for the click that followed. #601-followup: `employeeCount` switched from `equals: 1` to `changedBy: 1`, matching this project's own preferred convention for a running total (scenario-defs.md) and grid 3's own hire step (see its note) -- grid 1's driller now dies deterministically in both modes (see the preceding step's own note) and is never spliced in either one any more, so the baseline this hire step starts from is 1 (the corpse, never fired), not 0. `changedBy` proves what this step's own action did without pinning a baseline a future edit upstream would have to keep in sync by hand.

steps.description: #601: was `employee fire 2`. Grid 2's driller dies in its own blast deterministically -- confirmed via direct probe, `deathCount` reads 1 immediately after the preceding blast step in BOTH modes, run twice each for determinism, not the "command mode survives / interaction mode dies" split the old #599 note here claimed (that note was stale: written against an earlier build, it no longer matches this file's current behaviour). A dead employee has no row in #bs-employee-panel at all -- `.bs-detail-toggle` was never going to exist, in either mode -- but `fireEmployee` (Employee.ts) splices by id with no `alive` check, so the OLD command-mode script (a bare `employee fire 2`) could still fire a corpse a real player has no click for. That asymmetry is not benign: `runCommand`'s (createRunner.ts) action-count gate charges an action for ANY command that isn't specifically exempted, success or failure alike -- only `event choose` has a no-op exemption, `employee fire` has none -- so command mode's successful corpse-fire counted as one more action toward `MIN_EVENT_INTERVAL_ACTIONS` than interaction mode's genuine no-op (clickIfPresent finding nothing skips the console call entirely, contributing zero). One extra action, once, is enough: it opens a timer-event's cooldown gate one tick earlier in command mode than interaction mode, which trims that tick's `tick 50` call short in command mode but not interaction mode (events.ts's tick loop auto-pauses and `break`s the instant a timer event fires mid-block) -- and that single tick's worth of drift compounds every following chunk, ending 44 ticks apart by the file's own end (tick 391 command / tick 435 interaction, confirmed by direct probe) -- enough for interaction mode alone to cross REVOLT_TICKS and end in `worker_revolt` before ever reaching grid 3's blast. Fixing `fireEmployee`/`runCommand` themselves is out of scope for a scenario-JSON-only edit (and out of this session's permitted file list for this item) -- fixed here instead by making the two modes spend the identical (zero) action budget on this beat: `time resume` is genuinely idempotent this deep into an already-resumed run, and `time`/`tick` are META_COMMANDS, exempt from the action-count gate entirely in both modes, so neither mode's replay of this step nudges the cooldown gate at all. The one remaining real click -- opening the employees panel, so grid 3's hire step below still finds it open -- stays, modeling a player checking on their dead crew and finding nobody left to dismiss.

#596/#597: cash dropped from this checkpoint's own expect (was a hand-derived equals:161096) -- the cooldown-caching and event-pool-idempotency fixes (see the grid 3 tick chunks' own note) shift exactly which tick a random event goes pending on, and cycle 2's own chunks above now straddle that shift, so cash is no longer a value this observe step can pin without re-deriving it by hand on every future event-timing change. Same incidental-running-total class level1-win-efficient.json's own finances checkpoints already treat this way (cash absent from their equals blocks) -- a directional decreased/changedBy doesn't fit a read-only `finances` query either (before==after for the query itself; the spend already happened in the setup/action steps above it, which is where a directional cash check belongs, not here).

expect.note: #601: `employeeCount: 1` restored to this equals block. The prior note here (dropping it, #599-followup) was chasing a real but stale mode split from an earlier build ("command mode fires the survivor down to 0, interaction mode's corpse stays at 1") -- the step it blamed (`employee fire 2`) no longer runs a fire at all (see that step's own #601 note: it replays `time resume` in command mode and only opens the employees panel for real in interaction mode), so grid 2's driller -- dead in both modes, deterministically, confirmed by direct probe -- is never fired in either one. `employeeCount` reads 1 (the one corpse, never spliced) in both modes now, genuinely, not incidentally. #601-followup: corrected again, 1 -> 2 -- grid 1's own driller transition (see that step's own #601-followup note) is now fixed the identical way, so grid 1's corpse is never spliced either any more; this checkpoint sees both grid 1's and grid 2's corpses, never grid 1's alone. `vehicleCount` stays 0 regardless (the drill_rig is destroyed in the blast either way, driver dead or fired).

expect.note: a fired blast clears the plan back to zero; nuisance/ecology decrease again from wherever they'd drifted back to during the #553 drilling wait. #553: no longer asserting nuisance hits an exact floor of 0 -- that assumed blast 1 and 2's damage compounded with no recovery in between (pre-#553 drilling was instant, so all 3 blasts fired back to back); the real drilling waits between cycles now give scores real time to decay back toward baseline, so nuisance never actually reaches 0 by blast 3 -- decreased is what genuinely holds.

no fine, ever (Finding #9, see file description) -- cash only moves from the #553 driller hires/drill_rig purchases, payroll/upkeep during the 3 drilling waits, and one Explosive Embargo event during cycle 3's wait, not from any vibration-budget fine; cash itself stays absent from this checkpoint's own equals (see the earlier cycle-2 finances step's own note for why) rather than re-pinned to a new absolute figure. #601: employeeCount corrected from 1 to 2 (grid 2's driller, dead since blast 2, is never fired in either mode any more -- see that step's own note -- so their corpse plus grid 3's own live driller is 2, not 1) and tickCount corrected from 391 to 335. The #596/#597 note this superseded (391, up from 371) was itself chasing a real but different-root-cause drift; #601's own fix (see `employee fire 2`'s replacement step) closed a genuine command-vs-interaction action-count asymmetry that had been quietly costing interaction mode a timer-event's cooldown gate relative to command mode every tick after grid 2's blast, and grid 3's own tick budget above is trimmed from 4 chunks to the 2 its drilling now genuinely needs once that asymmetry no longer pads the count. #554: tickCount corrected again, 335 -> 595 -- charging is real work now too, and each of the 3 charge orders in this file is drained by its own wait step, adding real ticks on top of #553's own drilling waits. #601-followup: employeeCount corrected again, 2 -> 3 -- grid 1's own driller transition is now fixed the identical way (see that step's own #601-followup note), so grid 1's corpse is never spliced either any more; this checkpoint sees grid 1's corpse, grid 2's corpse, and grid 3's own live driller. tickCount is unaffected -- the action-count-gate asymmetry #601 traced was specific to the real command `employee fire N` executing in command mode with no interaction-mode equivalent, and grid 1's transition never spent that action in interaction mode either way (its old click chain no-op'd against a dead crew), so removing the command-mode-only splice does not change either mode's action count or tick trace. employeeCount/vehicleCount/buildingCount/holeCount/tickCount are all genuinely mode-invariant (unaffected by real-time host-timing drift, unlike cash) and still prove no fine mechanic fired -- a fine would need to either change cash outside the documented categories (not directly checkable here) or leave some other trace, and none of these structural counts would explain a cash discrepancy anyway; the remaining proof against a phantom fine is the finances breakdown itself, inspectable in the step's own console output.
